resources.description:
Zenith wet delay turbulence precursor of tropical-cyclone
convection (v2) 
Derived data and analysis code for the manuscript “Dense navigation-satellite networks time water-vapour reorganization hours before tropical
cyclone convection”. 
DOI of this deposit: https://doi.org/10.25835/9rps2gis Author names removed for peer review. 
Contents 
DATA/<storm>_sea.npz : per-storm superposed-epoch arrays. hrs is time in hours from closest approach; lam and lam_s the raw and
smoothed cut-off frequency in s^-1; sig the unsmoothed fluctuation amplitude in mm; lbase and sbase the pre-storm baselines.
DATA/<storm>_zwd.npz : network-median zenith wet delay on the same grid.
DATA/stations/<site>/*_maternfit.csv : per-station, per-day estimates. Columns: window-centre epoch (MJD), lambda (s^-1), sigma
(m), quality flag.
DATA/tracks/storm_<name>.json : best-track geometry, closest-approach time and distance for each cyclone.
QUIET/ : the storm-free summer record behind the false-alarm rate.
CODE/ : spectral estimator, onset and detector definitions, statistics and figure scripts.
SOURCE_DATA/ : one CSV per storm, as required by the journal. 
Spectral estimator 
Matern/von Karman spectrum with the slope parameter fixed at alpha = 1.3, so that only the cut-off frequency and the amplitude are estimated.
Sliding windows of 62.5 min (125 samples at 30 s), stride 5 min, Slepian tapers (NW = 4, K = 7), debiased Whittle likelihood. Two detrend stages: a
global Savitzky-Golay of order 3 over 125.5 min, then a first-order detrend inside each window. 
Raw observations 
Raw GNSS observations are not redistributed here. Hong Kong SatRef data are available from the Hong Kong Geodetic Survey after free
registration; NOAA CORS data are openly available from the NOAA National Geodetic Survey.
